title: Quantitative Model Substitution Likelihood & Rapid-Recovery Catalog
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: build a measurable index and companion catalog that predicts the likelihood a running customer workload will need a model substitution (substitution = automatic or manual fallback to another model variant/provider) within a 30-day window, and provide a prioritized rapid-recovery catalog of compatible substitutes and operational runbooks. This ticket scopes the PM deliverables, data signals, scoring approach, acceptance criteria, and stakeholder alignment needed to pilot the index with two enterprise customers and internal SRE/Support teams.

Rationale: with increasing model supply volatility, customers must be able to quantify substitution risk and pre-authorize recovery paths. This index turns vendor/variant availability, latency volatility, cost delta, and quality drift signals into actionable probabilities plus a ranked catalog of substitutions with rollback/runbook instructions.

Approach summary:
1) Define signal set and weights (availability, latency anomalies, pricing discontinuities, quantization compatibility, downstream eval drift, deployment affinity).
2) Ingest telemetry and external supply signals (public model releases, vendor status feeds, infra capacity projections) and normalize into daily indicators.
3) Train a lightweight probabilistic model (logistic regression + heuristics) to map recent signal windows to substitution events in historical playbacks.
4) Produce a per-model per-customer substitution likelihood score (0-100) and map to three risk tiers: Watch (10-29), Elevated (30-69), Critical (70+).
5) For models with Elevated+ risk, produce rapid-recovery catalog entries with: compatible model variant, expected latency/cost delta, quantization notes, required config changes, and validated regression test prompts.
6) Expose results in Console (model page) and to SRE runbooks/incident playbooks.

Key success criteria are captured below.
acceptance_criteria: Index is computed daily for >= 90% of active model-customer pairs with no more than 12h pipeline lag
Historical backtest (past 6 months) shows substitution-alert precision >= 0.6 at 'Elevated' threshold and recall >= 0.5 for Critical events
Pilot catalog contains at least 2 validated substitute entries per critical model for pilot customers
SRE runbook entries created and validated via a tabletop exercise with >= 3 runbook steps executed successfully
Console surface returns index score and suggested substitutes in the model details page and supports download of the catalog entry
deliverables: Spec doc: scoring method, signal definitions, and governance (Confluence)
Data pipeline manifest and sample normalized signals (CSV + schema)
Pilot substitute catalog (spreadsheet) with compatibility notes and test prompts
Console mock and API contract for score exposure
Runbook templates for automated and manual substitution flows
Pilot retrospective and measurement dashboard (precision/recall/MTTR impact)
risks: Signal sparsity for low-volume customers may produce noisy scores
Vendor status feeds may be unreliable or incompatible across providers
Quality regressions from substitution could increase support load if substitutes are not well-tested
Dependency on telemetry pipelines introduces operational coupling to infra teams
measurement_plan: Baseline extraction: identify substitution-like incidents from support logs across last 6 months
Backtest: compute ROC/precision-recall curves for candidate scoring models
Pilot A/B: enable catalog for two enterprise accounts and measure MTTR and customer-reported impact over 8 weeks
Dashboard metrics: daily substitution_score distribution, alerts generated, false positives count, MTTR following substitution recommendation
